A_target.statement:
The number of [[Definition:Rooted Tree|rooted]] [[Definition:Labeled Tree|labeled trees]] on $n$ vertices is $n^{n - 1}$.
Hence the number of labeled trees is $n^{n - 2}$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be a [[Definition:Formal Power Series|formal power series]] with $\map \Phi 0 \ne 0$, and let $T$ be the unique power series with $T = x \map \Phi T$ and zero constant term.
Then:
:$\sqbrk {x^n} T = \dfrac 1 n \sqbrk {u^{n - 1} } \map \Phi u^n$
This is the [[Lagrange Inversion Theorem]].

substitutions.the series T: the exponential generating function of rooted labeled trees

object_map.reformulation: Encode the recursive structure of rooted trees as the fixed point equation T = x e^T and solve it by Lagrange inversion.

validity_conditions: A rooted labeled tree is a root together with an unordered set of rooted subtrees, which is what gives exp(T).
The fixed point equation has a unique formal solution, as each coefficient is determined by lower ones.
proof_plan:
Let $\map T x = \displaystyle \sum_n t_n \frac {x^n} {n!}$, where $t_n$ counts rooted labeled trees.
A rooted tree is a root together with a set of rooted subtrees, so $T = x e^T$.
This is the fixed point equation $T = x \map \Phi T$ with $\Phi = \exp$, which has a unique formal solution.

By the source result:
:$\sqbrk {x^n} T = \dfrac 1 n \sqbrk {u^{n - 1} } e^{n u} = \dfrac 1 n \cdot \dfrac {n^{n - 1} } {\paren {n - 1}!} = \dfrac {n^{n - 1} } {n!}$
